question: What does the directly retrieved NAST proceedings abstract establish about the Labac crustacean study, and what does it leave unresolved?

source.title: Crustaceans as Bioindicators of Water in Labac River of Cavite
source.provider: National Academy of Science and Technology Philippines (DOST-NAST); Cavite State University
source.citation: Transactions of the National Academy of Science and Technology (Philippines), Vol. 33, No. 1, Poster Session BS-25, printed pp. 91–92. The volume is titled 2011; the NAST catalog page gives portal publication date 21 July 2015; the DOST-STII PSTA July–December 2013 issue lists item 0148.
source.authorNameDecision: Preserve source-specific variants; do not normalize author spellings or infer the relationship among names without a better bibliographic authority.

access.method: Official NAST-hosted PDF text and official volume catalog page reviewed online. No sign-in, download, contact or access-control bypass was used.

evidenceAssessment.abstractReports: Quantitative crustacean occurrence assessment at eight Western Labac sites and nine Eastern Labac sites. It describes shrimp and crab groups and summarizes environmental observations, but provides no scientific crustacean names or station-by-station results.
supports: Historical research was conducted at source-described Western and Eastern Labac sections.
The abstract provides an aggregate 17-site count and broad crustacean-group context.
doesNotSupport: Any fish species or fish occurrence
Scientific crustacean taxa, voucher-backed identities, abundance by station, or current presence
Station names, exact coordinates, collection dates, gear/method details, or site-to-waterbody geometry
Current water quality, water safety, catchability, fishing access, or legal rules
A Labac River/Labac-Alemang name or route crosswalk
Equivalence with the separate 2014 CvSU fish-presentation sample area or the 2009 thesis cited by a later CvSU paper
evidenceAssessment.historicalWaterMeasurements: The abstract gives aggregate narrative values (including a reported 2 ppt salinity), but provides no station allocation or current measurement. Do not convert these into a present-day salinity, safety or fish-presence claim.

relatedBibliographicLead.description: The references of the official CvSU Research Journal 2022 Cañas freshwater-shrimp article cite Dimero, D.N. (2009), “Crustaceans as Bioindicator of Water in Labac River of Cavite,” Graduate Thesis, CvSU Graduate School, 102 pp.
relatedBibliographicLead.relationshipTo2011Proceedings: Not established. Treat the thesis and proceedings abstract as separate records pending a primary bibliographic/catalog match.

rightsAndUse.decision: Treat as source-attributed abstract-level research context only. The public proceedings PDF is not an open reuse license; item-specific permission remains unresolved. Do not reproduce its full abstract or claim source data is openly reusable.

nextAction: If crustacean coverage is useful beyond the fish inventory, seek the separately cited 2009 thesis through authorized CvSU library or institutional access and verify its catalog identity, taxonomy, sampling details, and reuse terms. Keep fish evidence on its separate retrieval track.
